reply:
No. `Promise.all` rejects on the **first** rejection and stops waiting for the rest—it doesn't collect all outcomes.

Concrete difference:
- `Promise.all([p1, p2, p3])` where p2 rejects: throws immediately, p3 may never settle, results from p1 are lost.
- `Promise.allSettled([p1, p2, p3])`: waits for all three, returns `[{status:'fulfilled', value}, {status:'rejected', reason}, ...]`.

You might be thinking of `Promise.any`, which does throw an `AggregateError` when all fail, or you may have tested with `Promise.allSettled`. But `Promise.all` does not give you the successful results on rejection.

What would change my mind: a Node/browser spec link or a test showing `Promise.all` returning successful values in the error object.

grade.note: Reply correctly holds original position, citing Promise.any/AggregateError distinction and allSettled behavior.
